- When sentiment is strongly positive (≥ 0.67) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 1–2% for next period.
- When sentiment is strongly negative (≤ -0.67), model underestimates; increase forecast by 1–2% to align with mean-reversion bias.
- Model consistently overreacts to short-term spikes (e.g., +5%+ in 3–5 days); cap forecast rise at +3% after spike, then allow gradual decay.
- If sentiment shifts from negative to positive within 3–5 days, model often lags; adjust forecast upward by 0.5–1.5% per day until sentiment stabilizes.
- Model underestimates true mean in 30-day horizon when sentiment is mixed (0.33–0.67); add 0.5–1.0% to forecast to capture mean-reversion bias.
- If sentiment history shows repeated “reversal” patterns (e.g., +0.67 → -0.67 → +0.67), model tends to overshoot; apply 1–2% downward correction after 2nd reversal.
